blocks.text: I can describe what coal, oil and natural gas are, how they formed, and why they are non-renewable energy resources.

items.title: Coal
items.sub: How it forms from dead plants

items.title: Crude oil and natural gas
items.sub: How they form from dead plankton

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The break down of dead and decaying matter.
Organic matter comes from living organisms. It contains carbon atoms as the main framework of compounds to which hydrogen atoms can attach.
Fossil fuels are formed over millions of years from the dead remains of organisms.
Molecules made up of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

blocks.text: Coal, crude oil and natural gas are all {fossil fuels}. They are made from the dead remains of organisms over millions of years.
All three fossil fuels contain {hydrocarbons}. Hydrocarbons are molecules made up of hydrogen and carbon atoms **only**.
One example of a hydrocarbon is a molecule with two carbon atoms and six hydrogen atoms.

blocks.q: Which set of atoms could make a hydrocarbon?
blocks.why: Hydrocarbons contain hydrogen and carbon atoms only. A molecule that contains a sulfur atom is not a hydrocarbon.

blocks.text: Coal is a black, sedimentary rock. It is made of mostly carbon and hydrocarbons.
It may contain low amounts of impurities, such as **sulfur**.
Coal is a combustible (it burns) sedimentary rock because it is made mostly of carbon, with some impurities.

slides.title: How coal forms: swamps and peat

blocks.text: Coal forms over millions of years from dead trees and other plants. About 300 million years ago, in the Carboniferous period, the Earth was covered in swampy forests.
The dead plants became buried under layers of plant material and mud. The conditions were {anaerobic}, and this slowed down decomposition, so most of the carbon was kept.

blocks.label: What does anaerobic mean?
blocks.text: Anaerobic means without oxygen.
These conditions, along with high temperatures and pressure, led to the formation of peat.
Peat is a material made of partially decomposed organic matter (largely plant material) from waterlogged environments such as swamps.
Peat can be dried and used as a fuel. In some places it is used for heating, to cook food and to generate small amounts of electricity.
The layers of dead plants and sediment kept experiencing high pressure from the weight of the material above, and high temperatures from Earth.

rows.add: anaerobic conditions + high temperature + high pressure

rows.note: Peat is turned into hard, carbon-rich coal.

items.q: Why did the anaerobic conditions matter?
options: They slowed down decomposition, so most of the carbon was kept
They turned the plants into plankton
Partially decomposed organic matter from waterlogged environments

slides.title: Crude oil and natural gas: plankton

blocks.text: Millions of years ago, dead {plankton} settled at the bottom of the oceans.
Plankton are microscopic, aquatic plants and animals. Aquatic means they live in water. There are two main types:
The dead plankton were covered in layers of mud and other sediment.

slides.title: How crude oil and natural gas form

items: Dead plankton settle at the bottom of the oceans.
The plankton become covered by sediments and mud.
High pressure from the sediments and rocks above, and high temperatures from the Earth, turn the dead plankton into crude oil and natural gas.
The crude oil and natural gas move through the pores in sedimentary rock.
Reservoirs of crude oil and natural gas form under impermeable rock.

blocks.text: Crude oil and natural gas are found in the pores (little holes) in sedimentary rocks. They move through the pores until they reach {impermeable} rock, which they cannot pass through.
They gather in reservoirs below the impermeable rock.
To extract them, companies drill down through the impermeable rock to the reservoirs below. This can be done from land drilling rigs or offshore drilling rigs.

blocks.q: Sort each clue: does it describe coal, or crude oil and natural gas?

items.text: Starts as dead trees and other plants in swampy forests
Passes through a stage called peat
Starts as dead plankton on the ocean floor
Found in the pores of sedimentary rock
Gathers in reservoirs below impermeable rock

slides.title: Why we burn them, and why they will run out

blocks.text: The organic matter that forms coal, crude oil and natural gas decomposes into hydrocarbons.

Hydrocarbons can react with **oxygen** in combustion reactions. These reactions release large amounts of energy, which makes fossil fuels useful. We burn them to generate electricity, in vehicles and to cook our food.
Fossil fuels will eventually run out. They are **non-renewable** energy resources: they take millions of years to form and are being used at a faster rate than they are produced.

blocks.q: Is each statement true or false?

items.q: Crude oil and natural gas formed from dead plankton mixed in with sediments.
Oil and natural gas are found in the pores of igneous rock.
Coal is formed from deep sediments of organic matter made of prehistoric plants.
Fossil fuels are produced faster than we use them, so they are renewable.
Hydrocarbons react with oxygen in combustion reactions and release energy.

items: Coal is a sedimentary rock that burns because it is made mostly of carbon, with some impurities.
Coal is formed from deep sediments of organic matter made of prehistoric plants.
Oil and gas formed from dead plankton mixed in with sediments that formed millions of years ago.
Oil and natural gas are found in pores of sedimentary rock.
The organic matter that formed coal, oil and natural gas decomposed into hydrocarbons.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Formation of fossil fuels
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word, a number or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: Dead swamp plants are buried and, in anaerobic conditions with high temperature and pressure, form a material. What is this material called?
questions.explanation: Dead plants become peat first. Continued heat and pressure then turn peat into coal.

questions.prompt: What does the word anaerobic mean?
Hydrocarbons are molecules made of hydrogen atoms and which other type of atom only?
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons contain hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

questions.prompt: Coal may contain low amounts of an impurity named in this lesson. It is an element that starts with the letter s. What is it?
questions.explanation: Coal may contain low amounts of impurities such as sulfur.

questions.prompt: Crude oil and natural gas were formed from dead what?
questions.explanation: Crude oil and natural gas formed from dead plankton mixed in with sediments.

questions.prompt: Phytoplankton are plankton that are plants. What are plankton that are animals called?
questions.explanation: The two main types of plankton are phytoplankton (plants) and zooplankton (animals).

questions.prompt: Crude oil and natural gas gather in reservoirs below which type of rock, which they cannot pass through?
questions.explanation: They move through the pores in sedimentary rock until they reach impermeable rock.

questions.prompt: Hydrocarbons react with which gas in combustion reactions?
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons react with oxygen in combustion reactions to release energy.

questions.prompt: Are fossil fuels renewable or non-renewable?
questions.explanation: They are used at a faster rate than they are produced, and they take millions of years to form.

questions.prompt: About how many million years ago was the Earth covered in the swampy forests that formed coal? Give the number only.
questions.explanation: The swampy forests were about 300 million years ago, in the Carboniferous period.
